title: Erdoğan Ties Fund-Crisis Cleanup to Soma Mine Accountability as September Exports Set a Record
subhead: Ankara promises fast, 'just' resolution of the collapsed investment-fund sector and prosecutions over the Soma mine disaster, even as Türkiye posts its best September export figure ever and TUSAŞ signals the KAAN fighter's next prototype could fly within weeks.

sections.heading: Erdoğan Pledges Fast, 'Just' Fix for the Fund Crisis
sections.body:
Speaking at the opening of a 2,000-bed hospital in Şanlıurfa on Oct. 3, President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan said the government is working to resolve Türkiye's investment-fund crisis 'swiftly on the basis of justice and fairness, without allowing anyone's rights to be violated.' He said the State Supervisory Board (DDK), the Justice Ministry and the Treasury and Finance Ministry were taking the necessary steps, with a Fund Coordination Board overseeing the process, and promised that anyone who made unlawful gains would face accountability, according to Hürriyet Daily News.

Erdoğan's first stated priority was preventing harm to the economy, and he insisted that 'Türkiye's economy has the capacity to overcome this problem.' The remarks come after regulators ordered the liquidation of roughly 131 funds worth about $17 billion managed by seven asset managers — a collapse that Middle East Eye has reported affects around half a million people, many believed to be ruling-party voters, with some accounts down as much as 90 percent.

The president's intervention marks a shift from regulatory handling to a direct political commitment, an attempt to cap the fallout after the resignation of AKP deputy chair Fatma Betul Sayan Kaya over opposition accusations that she profited from share sales ahead of a Sept. 16 market sell-off.
sections.whyItMatters: Erdoğan is now personally owning the outcome, which signals that the fund collapse has become a retail-investor and voter-confidence problem the government cannot treat as a technical regulatory matter. How compensations are structured will determine whether the damage stays contained or feeds a broader trust deficit in Turkish capital markets.

sections.heading: Soma Mine Disaster: Five Dead, Nine Detained, Dual Probes Underway
sections.body:
Erdoğan also vowed that anyone responsible for a deadly mine collapse in Soma, in the western province of Manisa, would be held accountable. Five miners were killed and two others rescued with injuries in Thursday's collapse. Daily Sabah reported that the Energy and Natural Resources Ministry has launched an administrative investigation while the Soma Chief Public Prosecutor's Office has opened a judicial inquiry, and that nine people, including company officials, have been taken into custody.

'Anyone found to have been negligent or guilty will certainly be held accountable. We will also follow the process closely,' Erdoğan said at TEKNOFEST Southeast in Şanlıurfa. Soma carries heavy political weight: the same district was the site of Türkiye's worst mining disaster in 2014, when 301 workers died.
sections.whyItMatters: A fresh fatal accident at Soma revives one of the most politically charged labor-safety failures in modern Turkish history. The speed and outcome of the two-track investigation will be read as a test of whether accountability promises carry real weight or are damage control.

sections.heading: September Exports Hit a Record $26 Billion
sections.body:
Trade Minister Ömer Bolat announced on Oct. 3 that Türkiye's goods exports rose 15.4 percent year-on-year to $26 billion in September — the highest figure ever recorded for that month and the second-highest monthly total on record, after December 2025, per Hürriyet Daily News.

First-nine-month exports climbed 5.2 percent to $211 billion, and the 12-month total through September reached a record $283.7 billion, already exceeding the government's $282 billion full-year 2026 target. Imports rose 5.9 percent to $31.2 billion in September, but the monthly trade deficit narrowed 24.8 percent to $5.2 billion, with exports covering 83.2 percent of imports.

The cumulative picture is less bright: the January-September deficit widened 5.8 percent to $71 billion. Bolat said the government aims to keep the full-year shortfall below $100 billion despite higher energy costs tied to the conflict in the Gulf, and forecast current-account surpluses for August and September. He also flagged record bilateral trade with Poland at $12.5 billion in 2025, with talks covering the Türkiye-EU customs union and cooperation in energy, logistics and defense.
sections.whyItMatters: Strong export momentum — especially with the 12-month figure already beating the annual target — gives Ankara fiscal breathing room as it manages the fund crisis and elevated energy import costs. The unresolved issue is the widening cumulative deficit, which energy prices keep pressuring.

sections.heading: TUSAŞ: New KAAN Prototype Could Fly Within Weeks
sections.body:
TUSAŞ general manager Mehmet Demiroğlu said the P1 prototype of Türkiye's KAAN national fighter jet has completed system checks and low-speed taxi tests and could make its first flight in October or November if high-speed taxi trials proceed without setbacks, Anadolu Agency reported from the TEKNOFEST festival in Şanlıurfa. The earlier P0 aircraft made KAAN's maiden flight in 2024; work on a P2 prototype continues.

Demiroğlu also detailed TUSAŞ's broader pipeline: series production of the Hürjet jet trainer has begun, with deliveries to the Turkish Air Force scheduled for late 2027 and to Spain in late 2028. Two Hürjet prototypes have logged more than 600 flight hours, and a third flew in September. In September TUSAŞ signed a contract to supply Azerbaijan with 14 Hürkuş-II turboprop trainers, drawing on aircraft being produced for the Turkish Air Force to speed delivery. The company plans to outsource about 70 percent of production while retaining final assembly, and aims to deliver two Hava SOJ electronic-warfare aircraft in 2027.
sections.whyItMatters: A KAAN test flight would move Türkiye's flagship fifth-generation fighter program from prototype toward validation, reinforcing Ankara's bid for defense-industrial autonomy. The Spain Hürjet order and Azerbaijani Hürkuş deal show exports are broadening beyond drones into trainers — a more durable sign of the sector's maturity.

sections.heading: Trump Says No Obstacle to Lifting CAATSA Sanctions — Again, No Timetable
sections.body:
Asked at the White House on Oct. 2 why CAATSA sanctions on Türkiye remain despite his July pledge to remove them, President Donald Trump said there was 'no obstacle' to lifting the measures and reiterated his friendship with Erdoğan: 'I'll always speak to President Erdoğan. He is a friend of mine... And I'll always make him happy,' Hürriyet Daily News reported. He gave no timetable.

The sanctions, imposed in December 2020 over Ankara's purchase of Russian S-400 air-defense systems, target Türkiye's Defense Industries Agency (SSB) and several officials. Trump first promised removal at the July 7 Ankara talks and repeated it at the July NATO summit.
sections.whyItMatters: Trump's repeated verbal commitment without action leaves the SSB and Turkish defense procurement under a standing legal constraint that complicates co-production and export deals with Western partners. The gap between rhetoric and policy remains the operative fact for Turkish defense planners.

sections.heading: Türkiye, Georgia and Azerbaijan Deepen Trilateral Defense Ties in Shusha
sections.body:
Defense Minister Yaşar Güler attended the 13th trilateral defense ministers' meeting of Türkiye, Georgia and Azerbaijan on Oct. 2 in Shusha, Azerbaijan, alongside Irakli Chikovani and Zakir Hasanov. Güler said 'the security of the Caucasus cannot be considered separate from the security of Türkiye, Azerbaijan and Georgia,' and commended the normalization between Armenia and Azerbaijan, according to Hürriyet Daily News.

On the diplomatic side, Turkish and Georgian education ministers signed a cooperation agreement in Tbilisi on Oct. 2 covering reciprocal educational institutions, language teaching and diploma recognition. Güler called the trilateral partnership a 'multidimensional strategic cooperation' with special importance for energy, transport and communications security.

Separately, Erdoğan marked Turkic States Cooperation Day (the 17th anniversary of the 2009 Nakhchivan Agreement), and the Foreign Ministry confirmed Türkiye will host the Organization of Turkic States' 13th summit in Ankara on Oct. 29-30.
sections.whyItMatters: As Armenia-Azerbaijan normalization advances, Ankara is locking in a three-way security and connectivity bloc with Baku and Tbilisi that positions Türkiye as the transport and energy hinge of the South Caucasus. The October OTS summit will be the venue to convert that into concrete trade and logistics commitments.

sections.heading: Horn of Africa: Somaliland Courts Israel Explicitly to Counter Türkiye
sections.body:
Middle East Eye reported that Somaliland officials say their diplomatic normalization with Israel in January 2026 was partly motivated by the need to check Türkiye's growing military footprint in neighboring Somalia. A senior foreign-affairs adviser to Somaliland's president told MEE: 'We need air defense systems... Türkiye has F-16s in Mogadishu, and it wants to build a drone base in Somalia. We want Israel to support us against Turkey.'

MEE notes that Israel and Türkiye are competing for influence across the region — including in Syria — and that the Horn of Africa could become a testing ground because it sits outside the main spotlight. Somaliland officials were also notably less hostile toward Yemen's Houthis than Israel is, saying 'the Houthis need to be engaged.'
sections.whyItMatters: This is a new front in the Israel-Türkiye rivalry: Ankara's military presence in Somalia is now drawing a counter-alignment through Israeli recognition of Somaliland. It raises the risk that Red Sea shipping-security politics become entangled with the Turkish-Israeli competition, well beyond Syria.

bottomLine: Türkiye spent Oct. 3 projecting both economic resilience and accountability: record September exports of $26 billion, a new KAAN prototype nearing flight and an expanded South Caucasus defense bloc, set against Erdoğan's public promises to fix the $17 billion fund collapse and prosecute the Soma mine deaths. The domestic test is whether those promises translate into real compensation and prosecutions rather than reassurance. Abroad, Ankara is deepening its Caucasus and Turkic-world ties while a standing US CAATSA sanction it was told would be lifted still sits in place — and a new Israel-backed Somaliland alignment now shadows Turkish influence in the Horn of Africa.
sources: Hürriyet Daily News, Daily Sabah, Anadolu Agency, Middle East Eye, İhlas News Agency (via Hürriyet Daily News), Bloomberg (fund scale, previously reported), Reuters (context)
